title: The two poles of libidinal investment

techniques.name: Diagram of an argument

ground.label: Ground
ground.note: What the figure is drawn on: a blank sheet or ruled graph paper.

pitch.label: Grid pitch
pitch.note: Graph-paper square, in figure units. Acts with Ground on Graph paper.

hatch.label: Tone
hatch.note: How a toned shape is filled: solid ink, or the same tone laid as hatching.

gap.label: Hatch spacing
gap.note: Distance between hatch lines, in figure units. Acts with Tone on Hatched.

angle.label: Hatch angle
angle.note: Direction of the hatch lines. Acts with Tone on Hatched.

weight.label: Line weight
weight.note: Every stroke of the figure at this multiple of its measured width.

hand.label: Hand
hand.note: How far a line may wander from its ruled path, in figure units. 0 is ruled; higher redraws every line, box and pole by hand.

node.label: Node size
node.note: Radius of every node dot, as a multiple of its measured size.

type.label: Type size
type.note: Every label at this multiple of its measured size, from its own anchor. Held to the range where no label meets a line or the edge of the sheet.

lead.label: Leading
lead.note: Line spacing inside a label of several lines, as a multiple of the measured spacing; the first line holds its place.

techniques.implementation: Each claim of the text is drawn as boxes, poles and arrows on a white sheet with a numbered caption. The geometry is measured from the source figure; the engine redraws it, and each dial is a decision of the drawing that the figure has: ground, line weight, hand, box corners, dashes, nodes, arrowheads, tone and the setting of the labels.

techniques.name: Measured inks
techniques.implementation: solid ink pixels of each figure, read at full resolution, are clustered to five colors; a color is kept when it holds at least 4% of the ink.

techniques.name: Figure and ground
techniques.implementation: The ground is the most common border color of a figure; ink is every pixel more than 40 levels from it.

pass_order: line · every stroke, ruled or by hand
